text:
ashley: Ran a focused KV-quant run this morning (model: phi-13b-open, variants: fp16 baseline, fp8-kv, int8-kv, awq-kv) over our 10k prompt set. Summary: int8-kv -> -42% RAM on host, p95 cold-start jump 65ms -> 210ms, avg token latency +12%, eval BLEU-ish metric down ~1.8-2.2% vs fp16. awq-kv similar memory but worse tail variance. fp8-kv looked best memory/latency tradeoff but noisy accuracy.

ravi: ugh that cold-start p95 is bad. Did you use persistent KV on disk or keep in shared RAM? any eviction logs?

ashley: persisted to mmap file (kv.pmem) + eager mmap load on startup. evictions were rare during run but there were a few reads that triggered page faults. stack trace snippet:
```
[2024-04-03T09:12:23Z] page_fault: file-backed page fault on kv-mmap, load_time=128ms
[2024-04-03T09:12:23Z] async_prefetch: started prefetch for shard 7
```

jordana: can you paste the bench command + config? want to repro locally.

ashley: bench command:
```
./bench/kv_quant_run.sh --model phi-13b-open --variant int8-kv --requests 10000 --warmup 200 --kv-persist mmap --prefetch 0
```
config snippet I used:
```
kv_persistence: mmap
kv_prefetch: 0
kv_cache_size_mb: 1024
batch_size: 8
quant_backend: awq
```
Note: I toggled quant_backend between gptq/awq/fp8 for runs.

bench-bot: quick metrics (int8-kv run): p50=12ms p95=210ms p99=340ms mem=3.1GB (vs fp16 mem=5.4GB) quality_delta=+0.020 NLL

ravi: that quality_delta +0.020 NLL is concerning. Is the delta concentrated on long-context prompts or on short instruction prompts?

ashley: mostly long-context where KV cache is used heavily. Short prompts were fine.

jordana: hypothesis: int8 dequant path introduces micro-stalls when rehydrating KV pages -> page fault + synchronous dequant = tail spike. Two quick mitigations: 1) preload mmap pages in hot shards on startup (prefetch >0) 2) keep KV persistent but store quantized bytes in contiguous chunks to avoid scatter reads.

ashley: tried prefetch=1 -> p95 drops to 95ms, p99 160ms. Memory +5% due to prefetch buffer. Accuracy unchanged (still +0.018 NLL vs fp16).

ops-bot: note created: INF-1124 "kv-int8-coldstart-tail" assigned to @jordana

jordana: another idea: use fp8 for KV store and int8 for compute kernels, or hybrid decode path: keep KV in fp8 to reduce conversion cost. AWQ's layout increases scatter, so AWQKV likely worse.

ravi: any kernel-level fixes? like reduce synchronous dequant in hot path?

ashley: filed PR with an async dequant path (wip) but need to benchmark. Patch: convert background dequant + small LRU to keep hot kv in dequanted format. rough patch:
```
-- on KV read: if hot -> return dequanted cache
-- else -> schedule dequant task and return quantized pointer
```

jordana: sounds good. for immediate rollback plan: pin model variant to fp16 for customer-facing route, enable int8-kv on internal-only routes until async dequant lands.

ashley: agreed. I'll open rollback ticket and snapshot the run artifacts (profiles, mmap dumps, traces). attaching profile: s3://redwood-infra/kv_runs/1723345567/

ravi: thanks. next steps: (1) run hybrid fp8-kv + int8-kernels sweep, (2) test prefetch sizing (0/1/4/8 shards), (3) end-to-end quality check on long-context eval set. I'll take (3).

ashley: I'll run (1) and (2) tomorrow morning and post results in this thread. :rocket:
